item.title: Registered full-time employment up 5% in 12 months, NSO says
item.description: Registered full-time employment reached 312,504 people in June 2026, up 5.0% year on year, according to the National Statistics Office. Private-sector full-time jobs rose 5.4% while public-sector employment grew 3.6%, and part-time primary jobs increased 7.2% to 38,250, with transport and storage and accommodation and food services leading job creation.
item.content:encoded:
Registered full-time employment reached 312,504 people in June 2026, up 5.0% year on year, according to the National Statistics Office. Private-sector full-time jobs rose 5.4% while public-sector employment grew 3.6%, and part-time primary jobs increased 7.2% to 38,250, with transport and storage and accommodation and food services leading job creation.

Sources: Malta Independent

item.title: Central Bank says Malta's financial system remains resilient
item.description: The Central Bank's interim financial stability report assesses the first half of 2026, finding the Maltese economy performing strongly on robust domestic demand, favourable labour market conditions and tourism. It flagged inflation upside risks, rising operating costs and the concentration of bank lending in property as structural vulnerabilities, while noting non-performing loans declined and stress tests supported the sector's resilience.

item.title: Ex-inspector told police of irregularities in imported-car inspections before odometer scandal
item.description: A former police inspector told the court he flagged irregularities in the way cars imported from Japan were inspected, with vehicle-release stamps appearing on paperwork before cars had been inspected. Testifying in the case against two car dealerships accused of tampering with odometer readings on more than 400 imported Japanese cars, he said his 2020 report on the matter reached Police Commissioner Angelo Gafà and that Transport Malta initially resisted taking over the inspections. He said no Transport Malta official was ever charged over the kilometreage-fraud scandal.

item.title: MCCAA and OHSA sign agreement on workplace product safety
item.description: The Malta Competition and Consumer Affairs Authority and the Occupational Health and Safety Authority have signed a memorandum of understanding to work more closely on product safety in workplaces. OHSA officers will report suspect equipment, machinery and passenger lifts to the MCCAA, which will in return provide technical support and coordinate training.

Sources: Lovin Malta

item.title: Abela defends Malta's economic model as Nationalist Party attacks population projections
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela told Parliament that Malta remains resilient despite cost-of-living pressure, inflation and rising taxes across Europe, and warned that a radical change to the country's economic model would have serious consequences for Maltese and Gozitan families. Opposition leader Alex Borg accused Abela and Finance Minister Clyde Caruana of being "used to luxury" and of contradicting each other over population projections, pointing to Caruana's paid report projecting a population of 800,000 by 2040, which Abela has publicly dismissed as unrealistic. Separately, the Nationalist Party said government-appointed experts, the Central Bank and the Finance Minister are all warning that the economy needs roughly 14,000 additional people every year, while the National Audit Office flagged fragmented government databases that complicate the compilation of population statistics.

item.title: €15 million for Marsa arts hub to be reallocated after archaeological finds
item.description: Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea confirmed in parliament that the €15 million allocated from EU funds for the Marsa arts and culture hub will be reallocated to other projects, with the original completion target now set to slip. Archaeological discoveries — including what has been identified as the largest Punic quarry ever found in Malta, Punic and Roman catacombs and a British-period water tunnel — were made after construction began in January 2026, and archaeological investigations are under way across the site.

item.title: Former soldier appeals eight-year jail term over racially aggravated hit-and-run
item.description: Lorin Scicluna, acquitted earlier this month of murdering Lassana Cisse Souleymane, has lodged an appeal against the eight-year prison sentence imposed for grievously injuring May Malimi in a February 2019 hit-and-run in Ħal Far. The 29-year-old had earlier turned down a plea bargain that would have seen him serve 30 years.

item.title: Stivala loses appeal over Cassola's Muscat 'payback' posts
item.description: The Court of Appeal, presided over by Judge Mark Simiana, dismissed developer Michael Stivala's appeal in his libel case against Arnold Cassola over three November 2022 Facebook posts about Muscat's consultancy deals. The court held the posts were protected honest opinion based on substantially true facts, confirming the Court of Magistrates' ruling of April 2025, with costs to be borne by Stivala.

item.title: €6.4m in tax refund cheques went uncashed in 2025, minister says
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana told Parliament that 60,847 of the 289,638 tax refund cheques issued in 2025 were never cashed, leaving about €6.4 million of the €29 million paid out uncollected. The uncashed total since 2018 stands at €26,247,798, with the 2025 figure the highest in that period.

item.title: Only two of 105 government schools have a non-EU pupil majority
item.description: Education Minister Byron Camilleri told Parliament that St Theresa College Msida Primary (273 of 511 pupils) and Maria Regina College St Paul's Bay Primary (377 of 722) are the only government schools where non-EU pupils form a majority. Across 105 schools and support centres there are 36,763 pupils, of whom 7,750 are non-EU.

item.title: Audit Office flags fragmented databases behind Malta's population statistics
item.description: The National Audit Office told Speaker Carmelo Abela that fragmented information flows, inconsistent validation and reliance on manual processes complicate how the National Statistics Office compiles population data from four public entities. The review covered the governance and operational arrangements behind the NSO's use of administrative records.

item.title: Malta wins EU priority for underwater cultural heritage in 2027–2030 work plan
item.description: Malta's proposal was approved at a meeting of the EU Council on Education, Youth, Culture and Sport in Brussels, attended by Minister for Arts, Culture and National Heritage Malcolm Paul Agius Galea. The plan covers protection, conservation, restoration and promotion of underwater cultural heritage as part of Europe's identity.

item.title: Four Heritage Malta workers plead not guilty over duplicate ticket fraud case
item.description: Ryan Bonnici, Brian Castillo, Tonio Cauchi and Godwin Joseph Zarb pleaded not guilty to computer misuse, unauthorised copying and data extraction, data tampering, identity fraud, criminal association and illegal profit at Heritage Malta's expense. A cybercrime inspector testified that intercepted WhatsApp chats about a replaced printer at St Paul's Catacombs and duplicate tickets were the only evidence against one of the accused.

item.title: Hunters' federation hits back at EU call for Malta to halt finch trapping
item.description: The Federation for Hunting and Conservation said trapping is authorised by derogations in other EU states such as Austria's Salzkammergut region, and that the French Council of State has dismissed challenges to decrees regulating clap nets for catching skylarks. The European Commission has given Malta two months to respond to a reasoned opinion over the Birds Directive derogation, after which the dispute could go to the European Court of Justice.

item.title: 1,394 abandoned vehicles removed from Maltese streets since January 2025
item.description: Transport Minister Chris Bonett told Parliament that 785 abandoned vehicles were removed last year and 609 between January and September this year, with notices fixed on cars in Mosta before removal. Removal follows an internal process that includes attempts to contact owners so vehicles can be regularised, and is handled by Transport Malta, the police and Lesa.

item.title: Repeat offender jailed 135 days, faces deportation after driving stolen car
item.description: A 21-year-old man was jailed for 135 days after stealing a vehicle and driving it in Ħal Qormi without a licence or insurance. The court noted his earlier conviction for the same type of offence and that he is in Malta illegally, with the prosecution insisting on an effective prison term. The case was heard at the law courts this week.

item.title: Pickpocketing reports fall nationally but rise sharply in Valletta
item.description: Figures tabled in Parliament show 302 pickpocketing cases were reported across Malta and Gozo between January and October 2026, with St Julian's recording the most at 109. St Julian's has fallen sharply from 475 cases in 2024 and 169 in 2025, while Valletta is moving the opposite way with 70 reports so far this year, ahead of Sliema on 26.

item.title: Maltese production among the winners at the Golden Knight film festival
item.description: Fabrizio Fenech's Unur, Fama u Glorja was among the winners at the 64th edition of the Golden Knight Malta International Film Festival, with actor Peter Galea taking the best actor award for his role. The film also won best editing at the Lift-Off Berlin Film Festival, was selected for the Stockholm Film Festival, and reached the Venice short film semifinals.

item.title: Speaker Abela reaffirms Malta's commitment to strengthening ties with China
item.description: Speaker of the House Carmelo Abela reaffirmed Malta's commitment to its relationship with China during a meeting with Peng Qinghua, vice-chairperson of the standing committee of China's National People's Congress. The two discussed bilateral relations covering politics, trade, investment, maritime and air connectivity, education, culture and research, with Abela saying the relationship is built on trust, mutual respect and ongoing dialogue. The meeting was part of continuing parliamentary diplomacy, and a Chinese delegation was also received at Parliament.

item.title: Two jailed for two years after six-day dinghy crossing from Libya
item.description: Two men who crossed from Libya to Malta in a dinghy were jailed for two years for illegal entry and for helping another to disembark illegally. The court heard that the three men, among them a 29-year-old Syrian and a 37-year-old Libyan, were caught at Wied iż-Żurrieq after a six-day journey in choppy seas, and that two kittens were found on the boat.

item.title: Momentum urges objections to seven-storey elderly home in Mosta
item.description: Momentum is urging residents to object to a proposed seven-storey elderly care home overlooking Wied l-Isperanza in Mosta, warning that the 117-room, 200-plus bed project would dominate the valley. The party said it first objected on 27 August and that the representation window closes on 11 December.

item.title: Two Pembroke public plots to become recreation area and dog park
item.description: Two plots of public land spanning more than 13,500 square metres in Pembroke are being devolved to the local council under an agreement signed with the Lands Authority, for a recreation zone and a dog park. Ministers Owen Bonnici and Alison Zerafa Civelli signed the deal, and Pembroke Mayor Kaylon Zammit said the council will deliver a dedicated dog park and an equipped barbecue area.

item.title: Planning Authority takes enforcement action over illegal restaurant in Floriana public garden
item.description: The Planning Authority began enforcement action after a small kiosk in the King George V public garden in Floriana was converted without permission into a restaurant with a large structure dominating the garden. The Floriana Local Council, which is responsible for the garden, has been named one of three contravenors in enforcement case EC/137/26, alongside the restaurant's owner and the Heritage Authority, with daily fines already being imposed.
